newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open mixed, benefit from U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open mixed, benefit from U.S. data.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened mixed in moderate trade on Thursday, with much of the trading technical in nature even as tame U.S. inflation data provided support for the market.

"The data are fairly benign for the market at this point in time. I think a lot of what you're seeing in the market right now is technical. There's some very technically illiquid aspects of the yield curve right now," said one bond dealer with a bank-owned brokerage.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.11 to C$119.11 to yield 6.534 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 11/32 to yield 6.60 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was seven basis points, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were slightly stronger after the U.S. Labor Department reported that the consumer price index rose 0.2 percent in July, in line with market expectations.

The Canadian market on Wednesday rallied with U.S. issues after a report showing that the U.S. producer price index fell 0.1 percent in July reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would keep rates steady this month.
Dealers said trading in the Canadian bond market has been largely technically driven, with strong demand appearing in the two-year portion of the yield curve.

"The two-years are also in a very difficult situation. The fours of 99 (4.0 percent bonds due March 15, 1999) are trading at approximately one percent on a repo basis. That would suggest an extreme shortage of those bonds," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc.
The Government of Canada 4.0 percent bond due March 15, 1999 fell C$0.05 to C$99.67 to yield 4.219 percent.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.02 to C$109.30 to yield 5.979 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.30 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 32 basis points from 37 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange rose 0.39 to 119.96 with 1,598 contracts changing hands.
